When the conductor pod is deleted, it comes back on its own, takes its place again as the one conductor, and carries on with the legs that were running.
An Update requested from the web moves the pod to the channel's newer image, and the legs that were running are not relaunched.
The conductor's identity can launch and manage legs and nothing else, and a call outside that scope is shown being refused.
A local conductor can take over from the remote one, and the remote one can be scaled to zero, following written steps that have been rehearsed once.

A merge to main that regenerates staging publishes a new staging-channel conductor image, and ./promote-prod.sh publishes a new prod-channel conductor image. Each image is labelled with the plugin version it carries.
If the newer image cannot start during an Update, the conductor keeps running on its old image, its leases stay held, and the panel shows the failed update and its reason.
The GKE ticket-disk sweep runs in the cluster as a CronJob every 6 hours under the conductor's identity, and the Mac mini's sweep launchd job is removed.
`harmony conductor start --remote` starts the conductor pod and returns once the registry shows it running remotely. `harmony conductor stop --remote` scales it to zero, and running legs carry on.
A leg launched by the remote conductor gets its GitHub App installation token minted inside the pod, and can clone, push and open a pull request.
The remote conductor's log can be read with `harmony conductor logs --source cloud` and from the conductor panel's log link.
The conductor pod runs only on the always-on system node, never on the leg pool, and no GKE system pod is left pending or evicted because of it.

A local conductor whose host file names its secrets starts with no conductor.env or daemon.env present, and reads HARMONY_API_TOKEN and the GitHub App key from Secret Manager (the boot-time resolver is mode-independent; an explicitly set env var still wins).
